title: Library Imports
content: Imports `Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.Adjugate` for the adjugate matrix, Cramer map, and determinant identities, plus `Mathlib.Tactic` for proof automation.
mathContext: The adjugate module provides `Matrix.cramer` (the Cramer linear map), `Matrix.mulVec_cramer` ($A \cdot \text{cramer}(A,b) = \det(A) \cdot b$), `Matrix.cramer_apply` ($\text{cramer}(A,b)_i = \det(A[\text{col}\,i \leftarrow b])$), and `Matrix.mul_adjugate` ($A \cdot \text{adj}(A) = \det(A) \cdot I$).

title: Type Variables and Assumptions
content: The formalization works over a commutative ring $R$ with a decidable finite index type $n$. `DecidableEq n` enables case splits on indices; `Fintype n` enables finite sums for determinants; `CommRing R` provides the algebraic structure for matrix arithmetic.
mathContext: Variables: $n$ is a finite type with decidable equality (so determinants are computable), $R$ is a commutative ring (so $\det$ is well-defined via the Leibniz formula $\det(A) = \sum_{\sigma \in S_n} \text{sgn}(\sigma) \prod_i A_{i,\sigma(i)}$). No field or invertibility assumed for the general results.

title: Cramer Component Formula (Wiedijk #97)
content: The $i$-th component of the Cramer solution vector equals the determinant of $A$ with column $i$ replaced by $b$: $\text{cramer}(A,b)_i = \det(A[\text{col}\,i \leftarrow b])$.
mathContext: cramer_component$(A, b, i)$: $A.\text{cramer}\,b\,i = (A.\text{updateColumn}\,i\,b).\text{det}$. Proved by `Matrix.cramer_apply`. This is the classical formula $x_i = \det(A_i)$ (before dividing by $\det(A)$). The `updateColumn` operation replaces a single column while preserving others.

title: Cramer's Rule — Main Identity
content: The fundamental identity: $A \cdot \text{cramer}(A, b) = \det(A) \cdot b$. This works even when $\det(A) = 0$, making it more general than the classical formulation. When $\det(A)$ is invertible, dividing by it yields the unique solution $x = A^{-1}b$.
mathContext: cramers_rule$(A, b)$: $A.\text{mulVec}(A.\text{cramer}\,b) = A.\text{det} \bullet b$. Proved by `Matrix.mulVec_cramer`. The identity $A \cdot \text{adj}(A) = \det(A) \cdot I$ applied to $b$ gives $A \cdot (\text{adj}(A) \cdot b) = \det(A) \cdot b$, and $\text{cramer}(A,b) = \text{adj}(A) \cdot b$. This is Wiedijk's 100 Theorems #97.

title: Solution When Determinant Is Invertible
content: When $\det(A)$ is invertible (via the `Invertible` typeclass): $A \cdot (\det(A)^{-1} \cdot \text{cramer}(A, b)) = b$. This is the classical Cramer's rule: $x_i = \det(A_i)/\det(A)$.
mathContext: cramers_rule_solution$(A, b)$ [Invertible $A.\text{det}$]: $A.\text{mulVec}(⅟A.\text{det} \bullet A.\text{cramer}\,b) = b$. Proved by rewriting with `mulVec_smul`, `cramers_rule`, `smul_smul`, and `invOf_mul_self`. The `Invertible` typeclass is more general than `Field`: it works in any ring where $\det(A)$ has a two-sided inverse.

title: Cramer Equals Adjugate Times b
content: The Cramer vector equals the adjugate matrix applied to $b$: $\text{cramer}(A, b) = \text{adj}(A) \cdot b$. This connects Cramer's rule to the classical adjoint matrix.
mathContext: cramer_eq_adjugate_mulVec$(A, b)$: $A.\text{cramer}\,b = A.\text{adjugate}.\text{mulVec}\,b$. The adjugate $\text{adj}(A)_{ij} = (-1)^{i+j} M_{ji}$ where $M_{ji}$ is the $(j,i)$-minor. When $A$ is invertible, $A^{-1} = \frac{1}{\det(A)}\text{adj}(A)$, so $x = A^{-1}b = \frac{\text{adj}(A) \cdot b}{\det(A)}$.

title: Adjugate-Determinant Identity
content: The fundamental identity $A \cdot \text{adj}(A) = \det(A) \cdot I$. This is the algebraic backbone of Cramer's rule, relating the adjugate to the determinant.
mathContext: adjugate_mul_self$(A)$: $A \cdot A.\text{adjugate} = A.\text{det} \bullet (1 : \text{Matrix}\,n\,n\,R)$. Proved by `Matrix.mul_adjugate`. The identity follows from cofactor expansion: $(A \cdot \text{adj}(A))_{ij} = \sum_k A_{ik} \text{adj}(A)_{kj} = \sum_k A_{ik} (-1)^{k+j} M_{jk}$, which equals $\det(A)$ when $i=j$ and $0$ otherwise.

title: Transpose Form (Row-Based)
content: Cramer's rule for the transpose: $\text{cramer}(A^T, b)_i = \det(A[\text{row}\,i \leftarrow b])$. Transposition swaps columns and rows, so column replacement on $A^T$ becomes row replacement on $A$.
mathContext: cramer_transpose$(A, b, i)$: $A^T.\text{cramer}\,b\,i = (A.\text{updateRow}\,i\,b).\text{det}$. Proved by `Matrix.cramer_transpose_apply`. Uses $\det(A^T) = \det(A)$ and the duality between row and column operations. Useful when the system $x^T A = b^T$ is naturally row-oriented.

title: Linearity of the Cramer Map
content: The Cramer map $b \mapsto \text{cramer}(A, b)$ is $R$-linear: additive ($\text{cramer}(A, b+c) = \text{cramer}(A,b) + \text{cramer}(A,c)$), homogeneous ($\text{cramer}(A, rb) = r \cdot \text{cramer}(A,b)$), and zero-preserving.
mathContext: cramer_add, cramer_smul, cramer_zero: $A.\text{cramer}$ is an $R$-linear map $R^n \to R^n$. The proofs use `A.cramer.map_add`, `.map_smul`, `.map_zero` — Mathlib defines `Matrix.cramer` as a `LinearMap` from the start. Linearity follows from multilinearity of $\det$ in its columns: the column being varied ($b$) enters linearly.

title: 2x2 System Example
content: For $\begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} e \\ f \end{pmatrix}$ over a field with $ad-bc \neq 0$: $x = (ed-bf)/(ad-bc)$, $y = (af-ec)/(ad-bc)$. Verified by applying `cramers_rule` with `inv_mul_cancel`.
mathContext: The example specializes to `Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) F` over a `Field F`. Uses $\det(A)^{-1}$ (field inverse) rather than $⅟\det(A)$ (Invertible inverse). The proof rewrites with `mulVec_smul`, `cramers_rule`, `smul_smul`, `inv_mul_cancel hdet`, `one_smul`.

title: Verification of Core Mathlib Lemmas
content: Uses `#check` to verify that the four core Mathlib lemmas (`mulVec_cramer`, `cramer_apply`, `cramer_eq_adjugate_mulVec`, `mul_adjugate`) exist and have the expected types. This serves as documentation and a guard against Mathlib API changes.
mathContext: The four checked identities form a complete picture: $\text{cramer}(A,b)_i = \det(A_i)$ (component), $A \cdot \text{cramer}(A,b) = \det(A) \cdot b$ (main), $\text{cramer}(A,b) = \text{adj}(A) \cdot b$ (adjugate), and $A \cdot \text{adj}(A) = \det(A) \cdot I$ (fundamental).
